parsed.why: Strong operating protections for facilities, public accommodations, healthcare and safe passage materially improve the local picture. They cannot remove the parent-level passport, entry-screening and national-facility exposures.

No local facility ban is documented, and enforceable discrimination protections offer some recourse. But protections are less comprehensive, hate-crime coverage is absent, and the parent-level traveler-facing restrictions remain.

The state adds a broad, enforced birth-sex facility restriction across government buildings and schools, with criminal-trespass consequences and little remedy. This universal exposure compounds the hostile national framework.

The state adds sustained hostile policy, including upheld care restrictions and denial of care in custody, alongside thin discrimination protections. No comparable general facility ban is documented; national border and document risks still apply.

Operating public-accommodation protections, accessible state documents, bias-crime enhancements and a shield for care-seeking visitors offer meaningful local protection. The national passport, screening and facility regime still caps safety.
